author: Times News
description:
As the US ramps up its military presence in the Middle East, this looks at a high-risk scenario: the potential seizure of Kharg Island, which handles the vast majority of Iran’s oil exports, and why it matters strategically, from its deep-water access for tankers to its protection by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. It explores the military reality, including how many troops the US might need, the risks of counterattacks from the Iranian mainland, and the challenges of holding the island under sustained fire, alongside the wider consequences, from regional escalation to potential disruption of the Strait of Hormuz, which could send global oil prices soaring.
